events.title: Fort Ticonderoga Captured
events.description: Ethan Allen and his Green Mountain Boys, joined by Colonel Benedict Arnold, took the British-held fortress at Ticonderoga, New York, in a surprise attack early in the American Revolutionary War.
events.significance: The victory gave the colonial forces valuable cannons, which were later hauled to Boston to help force the British out of the city.

events.title: The Indian Rebellion Begins
events.description: Sepoys serving in the British East India Company's army rose in revolt at Meerut, starting a widespread uprising against Company rule in India.
events.significance: The rebellion led Britain to dissolve the East India Company and place India under direct Crown rule.

events.title: The Golden Spike Completes the Transcontinental Railroad
events.description: At Promontory Summit, Utah, a ceremonial golden spike was driven to join the Union Pacific and Central Pacific lines, completing the first railroad link across North America.
events.significance: Coast-to-coast travel dropped from months to about a week, which sped up westward settlement and transformed the American economy.

events.title: Churchill Becomes Prime Minister as Germany Invades Western Europe
events.description: German forces launched their invasion of the Netherlands, Luxembourg, Belgium and France. The same day, Neville Chamberlain resigned and Winston Churchill formed a new British government.
events.significance: Churchill's leadership through the darkest early years of the war became a symbol of British resistance to Nazi Germany.

events.title: Nelson Mandela Is Inaugurated as President of South Africa
events.description: Nelson Mandela took the oath of office as South Africa's first president elected in fully democratic elections, after decades of imprisonment and struggle against apartheid.
events.significance: His inauguration marked the end of apartheid-era white minority rule and the start of a multiracial democracy in South Africa.
